claims.statement: Under the Waste Act, the service provider is the default producer of waste arising from construction, demolition, renovation, cleaning, maintenance or repair services unless the service contract provides otherwise.

Where records are required, the transferring holder prepares KPO before transport; the receiving holder records a different received mass when applicable; and KPO may be omitted when one holder is outside the record-keeping obligation.

The current exemption regulation is code- and annual-quantity-specific: examples include paper and plastic packaging up to 0.5 Mg/year, wooden or metal packaging up to 1 Mg/year, non-hazardous used equipment code 16 02 14 up to 0.1 Mg/year, and selected construction fractions at limits from 5 to 20 Mg/year. The table does not create a blanket contractor exemption.

A usable eligibility screen must combine the actual waste code, annual quantity, hazardous or special-stream status, and the service contract's allocation of producer status; trade label or company size alone is insufficient.

Since 1 January 2025, producers of construction and demolition waste generally must ensure segregation of at least wood, metals, glass, plastics, gypsum and mineral waste; the duty may be outsourced by a written contract, but the statute provides joint liability among specified holders and the contractor performing the duty.

Photovoltaic panels sit inside the separate Polish waste-electrical-and-electronic-equipment regime and are separately identified in collection and product-fee reporting, so equipment removals cannot safely be treated as ordinary construction-container waste.

BDO supports external-system integration through REST API keys, but a key is generated by an authorized BDO user, is tied to that user, and is created in the selected entity context with at least one module permission.
The public BDO registry can be searched without login or payment for authorized waste receivers by waste code and geography, providing a lawful starting list of potential collectors.

The public BDO registry is a qualification directory, not evidence of live container inventory, open slots, binding quotes, pickup performance, contractor handoff frequency or buyer demand; those fields must be obtained directly and contractually.

PGK Śrem's 2026 list shows real paid pickup events: clean-rubble containers cost 345-1,455 PLN gross and mixed renovation/construction containers 498-3,591 PLN gross; the largest mixed container includes 5 tonnes and charges 658.80 PLN gross per extra tonne, while some other-waste prices exclude disposal and are set during contracting.

MPGK Rzeszów's business terms make the reconciliation pain concrete: mixed waste up to 1 Mg is 1,800 PLN gross, excess mass is charged at 1,800 PLN/Mg, transport is 9.50 PLN/km, mis-mixing can add 1,500 PLN, and actual scale weight must be promptly corrected in BDO; BDO failure may trigger a 500 PLN contractual charge plus return of the waste and related costs.

Paid BDO administration exists separately from pickup: Ekopomoc lists 25 PLN per KPO with at least 24 hours' notice, 50 PLN for one-hour notice, 600 PLN/year for a five-KPO mini plan, and 200 or 400 PLN monthly higher-volume plans.

Low-priced software already substitutes for basic BDO automation: RLGSOFT publicly lists 29 PLN/month for 25 BDO cards, 79 PLN/month for 200 cards, and 194 PLN/month for 1,000 cards, including KEO automation at each tier.

Interzero directly offers an integrated substitute covering pickup ordering and scheduling, automatic KPO creation and correction through BDO, KEO automation, cost and quantity reports, document storage and outsourced environmental support.

Gruz Assistance self-reports online container ordering in every Polish city, access to hundreds of waste firms, more than 30,000 containers collected from businesses and complete BDO administration; the scale claims are vendor-reported, but the offer closely substitutes for the proposed booking-plus-BDO bundle.

The strongest possible wedge is not generic BDO entry but proof-before-pickup and estimate-to-scale reconciliation for contractors with frequent non-exempt handoffs, because basic KPO software is cheap and integrated pickup/BDO services already exist.

No sourced evidence identifies how many reachable PV, heat-pump, electrical or renovation contractors have at least one non-exempt, paid waste handoff per month after code thresholds and contract allocation are applied.

No sourced evidence establishes that these small contractors hold a separate software budget after free BDO, a chosen collector, office staff, low-cost BDO software and outsourced BDO administration are accounted for.
The economic buyer and approver—owner, operations lead, office administrator, accountant or main contractor—remain unidentified for the target segment.
Collector willingness to publish binding quotes and slots, return scale tickets promptly, accept a disclosed 4% or fixed booking fee, and support dispute workflows has not been evidenced.

The rate of wrong-code handoffs, weight corrections, rejected loads, contamination surcharges, empty runs and human support minutes in this contractor niche is unknown; public law and price lists do not supply those operating distributions.

BDO access authorization does not itself grant the venture a right to reuse contractor photos, customer-site identifiers, collector quotes, scale tickets or service-performance data across customers; controller/processor roles and contractual reuse rights remain unverified.

contrary_evidence: Many small-volume streams are exempt, and service contracts can change who owns the duty.
Basic BDO software and human administration are already inexpensive.
Interzero and Gruz Assistance already cover much of the proposed integrated workflow.
The public registry helps find collectors but not frequency-qualified contractor buyers.
Physical booking and dispute exceptions can erase software-like margins.

economics.acquisition_route: Months 0-3: family installer plus four unrelated contractors reached through its local network; qualify two collectors from the free BDO receiver search (S6). Thereafter test collector and electrical/HVAC-wholesaler referrals, budgeting 150-350 PLN cash-equivalent CAC per activated paid account including onboarding and partner share. Do not assume associations or field-service vendors distribute until one supplies at least 20 qualified leads and five paid accounts.
economics.capital_required_pln: 45,000-80,000 PLN before scale: 10,000-18,000 legal/environmental classification, terms, insurance and data work; 20,000-35,000 mobile workflow and BDO integration; 8,000-15,000 pilot travel, devices, support and collector onboarding; 7,000-12,000 contingency. Stay inside the founder's 100,000 PLN and do not use parents' additional 100,000 PLN unless the paid gates pass.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Snapshot-definition path, conditional rather than forecast: months 0-3, instrument 30 handoffs, obtain 10 paying contractors and two signed collectors; month 12, 100 accounts x 179 PLN = 17,900 PLN MRR; month 24, 500 accounts = 1.074 million PLN ARR; month 36, 1,000 accounts = 2.148 million PLN ARR; months 60-72, 2,300 accounts and about 4,600 pickups/month = 4.940 million PLN ARR. At a mature 25% EBITDA margin, EBITDA is 1.235 million PLN; at 5x EBITDA enterprise value is 6.175 million PLN. With 85% founder ownership, founder business equity is 5.249 million PLN. Add no more than 0.05 million PLN accumulated personal after-tax distributions while employed, subtract assumed zero personal business liabilities, and do not add retained company cash already reflected in enterprise value: founder net worth is about 5.30 million PLN, excluding the primary residence. While employed, reinvest 95% of after-tax distributable cash and cap distributions at 5%. The path fails if the business cannot reach roughly 2,300 active high-frequency accounts, 60% contribution before overhead and 25% EBITDA within five to six years.
economics.founder_time: Pilot budget 20-25 hours/week, within the founder's maximum five hours/day: about 8 hours product/data, 6 hours field observation, 5 hours collector/customer work and 3-6 hours support/legal review. Do not scale while the founder is the dispatcher; before 30 paid accounts require less than ten support minutes per completed pickup and no routine after-hours duty, then hire or contract operations when the queue exceeds 100 accounts.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Illustrative qualified account at two pickups/month: 99 PLN subscription plus 2 x 40 PLN average collector fee = 179 PLN monthly revenue. Target direct monthly costs are 12 PLN payments/hosting/messages, 20 PLN partner revenue share, 24 PLN support at 0.4 hour x 60 PLN/hour, and 10 PLN exception/refund reserve, leaving 113 PLN contribution or 63%. If manual coordination adds 0.5 hour per pickup, contribution falls to 53 PLN or 30%; at roughly one founder hour per pickup the model is uneconomic. Pickup and service price anchors are sourced (S7, S8, S11, S12); frequency, fee and support inputs are explicit inferences.
economics.payback: At the illustrative 113 PLN monthly contribution, a 300 PLN activated-account CAC pays back in 2.7 months; set a hard gate of no more than four months. This is arithmetic, not evidence: zero collector fee, one pickup per month, or more than 0.4 support hour per account materially lengthens payback.
economics.pricing: Gated inference, not observed willingness: 99 PLN net per contractor per month plus 4% of a platform-originated completed pickup paid by the collector and capped at 75 PLN. The subscription sits above RLGSOFT's 79 PLN/month 200-card tier but below Ekopomoc's 200 PLN/month mid-tier; the fee would average about 20-75 PLN across PGK Śrem's 498-3,591 PLN mixed-waste range (S7, S11, S12).
economics.retention_or_repeat: The viable segment must average at least one required paid handoff per month, with the base case assuming two. Require at least 80% twelve-month gross logo retention and 70% of customers using the workflow in each rolling quarter before calling it recurring; seasonal or threshold-exempt contractors are expected to churn. No retention cohort exists.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: A permissioned longitudinal dataset linking job type, contractual waste-producer role, waste code, photos, quoted price, estimated and scale weight, contamination reason, surcharge and collector service outcome can improve pre-pickup checks and quote accuracy; cross-customer learning is allowed only when contracts and data-protection terms permit it.
fingerprint.customer: Polish PV, heat-pump, electrical and renovation contractors with a verified minimum of one non-exempt paid waste handoff per month and an owner or operations buyer; exclude firms whose relevant streams remain under exemption thresholds or are contractually the customer's responsibility.
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Use the founder's family renewable installer for instrumentation, then require four unrelated contractors and two licensed collectors in one Wielkopolska cluster. Expand only through collectors or electrical/HVAC wholesalers that can supply named, frequency-qualified accounts; use the public BDO registry to qualify collector permissions, not as proof of buyer demand.
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: A mobile evidence, KPO-preparation and measured-weight-reconciliation workflow using customer-scoped BDO API access and human confirmation of codes. Start with each contractor's incumbent collector. Price at 99 PLN net per contractor per month; only after signed collector terms add a disclosed fee of 4% of the completed platform-originated pickup, capped at 75 PLN.
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The contractor pays the monthly fee only after a shadow pilot proves saved staff time or avoided pickup cost. A collector pays the capped booking fee only for a new, completed, platform-attributed pickup; existing contractor-collector transactions earn no fee.
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A qualified job creates a non-exempt stream for which the contractor is the contractual waste producer and must arrange a paid handoff: before transport it needs correct recipient, code and estimated mass; after weighing it may need mass correction, surcharge evidence or a rejection-resolution trail.

founder_fit: Direct access to the parents' seven-person renewable installer makes field instrumentation and workflow observation unusually cheap and credible.
The founder's data and automation skills fit a rules-assisted mobile workflow, API integration, reconciliation logic and quantitative pilot design.
A 45,000-80,000 PLN gated pilot fits the founder's 100,000 PLN available capital without relying on parents' additional capital.

The 5-hour daily limit fits product and analysis work but not continuous dispatch, collector chasing or contamination disputes; the concept is part-time compatible only if the pilot proves less than ten human support minutes per completed pickup.
Partner distribution suits the founder's lower appetite for constant direct networking, but no partner channel is yet signed and the family pilot risks false confidence from a trusted relationship.
risks: A wrong code suggestion or incomplete special-stream branch could create environmental, contractual and financial exposure even with a confirmation screen.
Low-frequency customers may pay for a pickup but not retain a monthly software subscription.
Collectors may refuse transparent comparison or a fee on accounts they already serve.
Incumbents can copy photo capture and measured-weight reconciliation or bundle them into existing service.
Manual quote chasing, rescheduling, contamination disputes and KPO correction can turn the product into a low-margin dispatch service.
The family company can validate usability but may overstate trust, access and willingness relative to unrelated buyers.
Unauthorized aggregation of customer-site or collector commercial data would destroy the proposed data advantage.
The founder cannot sustain routine on-call operations alongside a full-time role within the five-hour daily limit.
thesis: Serve only Polish installation contractors that can verify at least one non-exempt paid waste handoff per month. Begin as a contractor-side, human-confirmed evidence and BDO workflow tied to the contractor's existing collectors: capture job photos and contract allocation, prepare BDO fields before transport, reconcile estimated to scale weight, and preserve surcharge or rejection evidence. Charge a 99 PLN monthly workflow fee; add a disclosed collector fee only for platform-originated completed pickups after a collector signs binding quote, slot, data and fee terms. Do not build an open marketplace until transaction density and low-touch exception economics are demonstrated.
title: Mobile BDO handoff and weight-reconciliation workflow for high-frequency installation contractors
uncertainties: Monthly non-exempt handoff density and seasonality by contractor niche.
Separate contractor willingness to pay and the actual budget owner.
Collector take-rate, data-feed and service-level willingness.
Preventable correction, rejection and surcharge rates.
API onboarding completion, support burden and customer-scoped permissions.
Cross-customer data reuse rights and classification-liability allocation.
Partner-channel conversion and CAC outside the family network.
